verdict: Nvidia's revenue jumped 78% to a record $39.3B as Data Center sales nearly doubled — its new Blackwell chips shipped $11.0B in their first quarter — and it kept $22.1B as profit.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: AI data-center chips and networking — Blackwell systems shipped $11.0B in their first quarter; up 93% YoY.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: GeForce graphics cards for gamers and AI PCs — down 11% YoY on limited supply as the RTX 50 series launched.

segments.name: Professional Visualization
segments.note: Workstation graphics for designers and engineers; up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Chips and software for cars and robots — self-driving platform sales drove a 103% jump.

segments.name: OEM and Other
segments.note: Smaller chip sales to other manufacturers; up 40% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Spending to design future chips and AI software.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and day-to-day running costs.

follow100Note: Data Center alone is $90.47 of every $100 Nvidia takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are revenue by market platform, as NVIDIA reports them.
otherDetail: Interest income $511M, plus $733M of other income (mostly $727M of gains on equity investments), less $61M interest expense, net.

takeaways.title: Data Center did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit a record $35.6B, up 93% — about $90 of every $100 Nvidia took in — as cloud builders raced to install AI systems.

takeaways.title: Blackwell's first quarter
takeaways.text: The new Blackwell AI chips shipped $11.0B in their first quarter — the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history — with large cloud providers taking about half of Data Center revenue.

takeaways.title: Gaming took a breather
takeaways.text: Gaming revenue fell 22% from the prior quarter to $2.5B because both new and older graphics cards were in short supply, even as the GeForce RTX 50 series launched.
